text: Cut every word that carries no fact or no step; padding such as 'the fact that' goes first.
check: Each cut leaves the facts intact (facts-preserved), and no 'the fact that', 'in order to' or 'at this point in time' is left.

text: Use the active voice, so the reader sees who does what: 'I wrote 60 help articles', not '60 help articles were written'.
check: No passive sentence hides an actor that the original or the CV names.

text: Say the action with its verb, not with a noun hiding the verb: 'we analysed the tickets', not 'we conducted an analysis of the tickets'.
check: slop-lint OFI-01 does not fire where the genre turns it on; no 'conduct an', 'carry out the' or 'make a decision' before a noun in -tion, -ment or -ance.

text: Prefer the specific claim to the general one: a number, a name or a date from the CV says more than an adjective.
check: Every claim about results carries a figure, a name or a date that is in the original or the CV (no-new-facts).

text: Alternate short and long sentences; a run of sentences of the same length reads flat.
check: slop-lint EST-11 does not fire on a text of eight or more sentences.

text: Put the most important thing first, the request or the news, and let the detail follow.
check: The first sentence names what the writer asks for or reports; no 'I hope this email finds you well' before it.

text: Choose the short common word over the formal one: 'use' over 'utilise', 'start' over 'commence', 'enough' over 'sufficient'.
check: No formal word replaced a plain one of the original; the judge's register-fit rubric holds.

text: Write to the reader as 'you', one person to another, and drop throat-clearing such as 'please note'.
check: No 'please note', 'kindly be advised' or 'it should be noted that' is left.

text: Use the exact word, not a near one, and keep the style simple and straight.
check: No word of the original was swapped for a vaguer or fancier near-synonym.

text: Do not imitate the period language of the literary sources: no archaic words or eighteenth-century spelling.
check: S6 finds none of the terms; the judge's literary-contamination rubric flags any other archaism.

text: Take Twain's economy, never his dialect: no spelled-out accents, dropped letters or folksy grammar.
check: S6 finds none of the terms; the judge's literary-contamination rubric holds.

text: Take Bierce's concision, never his tone: no sneer, no scolding and no joke at the reader's expense.
check: The judge's register-fit rubric finds no sardonic aside the original did not have.

text: Do not build long periods of chained clauses; when a sentence carries two ideas, split it.
check: No sentence of the rewrite is longer than the longest sentence of the original.

text: Do not borrow the mood of a story: no melancholy, no lyrical scene-setting and no drama in a message about work.
check: The judge's literary-contamination rubric finds no tragic or lyrical turn the original did not have.
